subject: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — Next Steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@atlas-payments.com>, Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — Initial Recap

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet you both on the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scheduled:

Summary of objectives
- Validate Atlas Payments can route transaction-enrichment requests to Redwood with consistent latency and acceptable cost per inference.
- Verify model quality on your production prompts and ensure no regression vs. your baseline.

Proposed success criteria / KPIs to evaluate during the POC (please confirm or edit):
1) Latency
   - P95 latency for 32-token generation <= 300 ms (target) / P95 <= 350 ms (acceptable failover).
   - Cold-start first-token latency measured separately during sustained traffic.
2) Throughput
   - Sustained throughput target: 200 requests/sec for the endpoint profile (concurrent traffic pattern).
3) Cost
   - Cost per 1k input tokens <= $0.60 (goal) — we will provide detailed cost breakdown (tokens, batching) in the POC report.
4) Quality
   - Intent/classification top-1 accuracy >= 95% on your evaluation set (50–100 representative prompts).
   - Hallucination rate < 2% on sampled responses (manual review).

Ownership & timeline
- Atlas owner: Priya Iyer — provide evaluation dataset and point of contact for infra/ingestion.
- Redwood owners: Jordan Blake (sales / POC lead), Marissa Cole (CS for runbook & ops), Rishi Malhotra (SRE/benchmarks).
- Proposed POC timeline: 4 weeks
   Week 1: Integration + baseline collection
   Weeks 2–3: Run experiments (latency/throughput/cost) and quality evaluation; iterate on batching/quantization profiles.
   Week 4: Joint review, recap, and recommended next steps.

Attachments & links
- I attached a lightweight POC template (redwood_poc_template.docx) with the evaluation plan and metrics we will collect. Also linking a shared doc to capture the evaluation dataset: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cATLAS-POC-template

Next steps
- Priya: Can you confirm the evaluation dataset owner and whether the test traffic can be routed to a staging domain (staging.api.atlas-payments.com)?
- Alex: Please confirm if the 200 req/s sustained throughput target is representative of your expected peak for the test.
- Redwood: We’ll propose 3 x 1-hour slots for a kickoff once we have confirmation.

Thanks — happy to adjust the KPIs if you want different thresholds.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Green <alex.green@atlas-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — Initial Recap

Thanks Jordan — useful recap. A couple of quick tweaks/questions from our side:

1) Latency target: can we tighten the target to P95 <= 250 ms for the critical payment-lookup flow? That flow is latency-sensitive. We understand that may adjust cost or instance sizing.
2) Cost cap: Can we add a hard budget cap for the trial (e.g., not to exceed $6,000 for the 4-week window) so we can get internal approval quickly?
3) Data handling: we will send a separate note with the staging endpoint and any data handling constraints — we need to ensure logs can be disabled for PCI scopes.

We can provide the evaluation dataset next Wednesday (2027-11-17). Alex confirms 200 req/s is representative of the peak we expect for the test window.

If Redwood agrees to the tightened latency target and a soft budget-control mechanism, we can sign off on the POC and schedule kickoff.

– Priya
Priya Iyer
Head of Integrations | Atlas Payments
priya.iyer@atlas-payments.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@atlas-payments.com>, Alex Green <alex.green@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — Initial Recap

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks — we can accommodate the tighter P95 <= 250 ms target for the payment-lookup flow as long as we confirm expected concurrency shape and agree on instance sizing during week 1. We’ll include a cost-guard: Redwood will send weekly spend alerts and stop the trial if spend approaches 90% of the $6,000 cap unless you opt to continue.

Kickoff scheduling
- Proposed 3 slots (PST):
  • Wed 2027-11-17 10:00–11:00
  • Wed 2027-11-17 15:00–16:00
  • Thu 2027-11-18 09:00–10:00
Please pick one and we’ll circulate a calendar invite with a short agenda (integration checklist, baseline test plan, data/security notes).

Attachments
- I’ve attached a small CSV (latency-benchmark.csv) with the baseline micro-benchmark profile we’ll run during Week 1 to measure single-stream and batched performance.

Action items captured
- Atlas: deliver evaluation dataset by EOD Wed 2027-11-17 (Priya).
- Atlas: confirm staging domain / data handling constraints (Priya).
- Redwood: prepare test harness and cost-alert configuration (Marissa / Rishi).
- Redwood: confirm instance sizing recommendation after initial baseline run (Rishi).

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — happy to lock this in.

Confirmed:
- KPIs: P95 latency target for payment-lookup <= 250 ms (critical flow), throughput 200 req/s, quality thresholds as listed.
- Budget: $6,000 4-week cap with weekly spend alerts (Redwood will pause trial at 90% unless Atlas approves continue).
- Deliverables: Atlas provides dataset and staging domain by 2027-11-17 (Priya).

Kickoff: Alex and Priya selected Wed 2027-11-17 10:00–11:00 PST — I’ll send a calendar invite with the agenda and dial-in now.
